aristotle_evidence: Aristotle says terrain suited to horsemanship favors a powerful oligarchy because keeping horses belongs to large estate owners.
limits: Aristotle offers a constitutional theory, not a census of cavalry wealth or a rule followed by every polis.

resource_barrier: Self-equipping as a hoplite favored the well-to-do.
aristotle_evidence: Aristotle places heavy infantry between cavalry oligarchy and the more democratic light and naval arms.
limits: The cost and composition of hoplite service varied; hoplite warfare did not mechanically create political rights or democracy.

resource_barrier: Less personal equipment lowered the wealth barrier.
aristotle_evidence: Aristotle calls light infantry a democratic element because military usefulness extended below the hoplite property threshold.
limits: Poor citizens and non-citizens could serve; military participation was not identical to citizenship or an observed grant of voting rights.

resource_barrier: The polis supplied the ship; rowers did not need a private panoply.
aristotle_evidence: Aristotle classifies naval forces as democratic: a fleet made large numbers of less-wealthy men militarily indispensable.
limits: The source describes a political tendency, not the number, wealth, citizenship, or causal effect of rowers in any one fleet.
